solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Supply on street in county town

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another follows it, so the supply word comes after the street

parts.note: to afford is to supply or provide

explanation.surface: Someone is delivering provisions along a road in a county's main town.
explanation.definitionFit: Stafford is the county town of Staffordshire in the English Midlands, its administrative seat.

indicators.note: tailless means the last letter, the tail, of the creature is cut off

parts.note: a scorpion is an arachnid, like spiders

explanation.surface: A sign showing an arachnid without its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: Tailless scorpion is apt, since its tail carries the sting.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorpio is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

indicators.note: releasing the fine letter lets it go from the agent word

parts.note: a factor is an agent who buys and sells for another
F is the pencil abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: An agent lets go of a good performer.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor is a player on stage, the older theatrical sense of player.

clue.text: Quick to collect barking setter in London thoroughfare

parts.note: fleet means swift or quick

indicators.note: barking means mad, so the letters of setter are scrambled

explanation.surface: A barking dog of the setter breed is grabbed quickly in a London street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barking' is British slang for mad, used here as the anagram signal, not a dog's noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleet Street is a London street long synonymous with the national newspaper press.

indicators.note: the others word goes around the island letters

parts.note: the rest are the others

explanation.surface: People on an island oppose the others around them.
explanation.definitionFit: To resist is to oppose or withstand something.

clue.text: Streetcar runs behind time in the morning

indicators.note: the runs letter sits behind, that is after, the time letter

parts.note: R is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for runs
a.m. marks times in the morning

explanation.surface: A streetcar service runs late in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: A streetcar is the American term for a tram, a passenger vehicle running on rails along roads.

indicators.note: the list word contains the duck letter inside it

parts.note: a roster is a list of duties or names
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, the shape of O

explanation.surface: A poultry list includes both a duck and a cockerel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' looks like a bird beside 'cock' but is the cricket score of zero.
explanation.definitionFit: A rooster is a male domestic fowl, the bird also called a cock.

parts.note: arch means chief or leading, as in arch-rival

explanation.surface: A man is heading a protest.
explanation.definitionFit: A march is a protest walk through the streets, a form of public demonstration.

indicators.note: an odd arrangement of the letters of route signals that they are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A strange path someone takes is described as unconventional.
explanation.definitionFit: Outré is a French borrowing for bizarre or beyond accepted norms, a synonym of unconventional.

clue.text: One taken in, reportedly, to get help

indicators.note: reportedly says the word is as heard spoken, not as written

parts.note: someone taken in, that is fooled, is a sucker

explanation.surface: A dupe is said to be seeking assistance.
explanation.definitionFit: Succour is a rather formal word for assistance given in time of need.

clue.text: Pile of fertiliser, inexpensive — order by mail received

indicators.note: the inexpensive word receives the other letters inside it

parts.note: cheap means inexpensive
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour
post is mail

explanation.surface: Cheap fertiliser is ordered by mail and delivered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'received' puts OMPOST inside CHEAP after its C.
explanation.definitionFit: A compost heap is a garden pile of rotting material that becomes fertiliser.

indicators.note: not quite the whole word means its final letter is dropped

parts.note: an actor's role is a part

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether an ordinary role is quite what it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: Par is the standard or average level, so 'on a par' means normal; as a noun it fits 'Normal' used as a noun.

clue.text: Striker on trial for big game

indicators.note: the striker word follows the trial word, placed on it in the across reading

parts.note: a test is a trial
a match is struck to light it, so it is a striker

explanation.surface: A football striker is being given a trial ahead of an important game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striker' suggests football, but here it is a match you strike. A Test match is a full international cricket fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: A Test match is a major international fixture in cricket or rugby, so a big game.

indicators.note: letters that are travelling move about, so the word poor is rearranged

explanation.surface: A poor person is journeying to a city in Portugal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling' makes OPOR from POOR, then TO is added as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Oporto is the English name for Porto, Portugal's second city, famous for port wine.

indicators.note: excited suggests the letters of her opus are agitated into a new order

explanation.surface: A legendary musician was thrilled by a woman's composition.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Orpheus played the lyre so beautifully that he charmed animals and even the underworld.

indicators.note: the pole word comes chasing, so after, the stolen word

parts.note: stolen goods are said to be hot
a rod is a pole

explanation.surface: A Polish person is pursuing a stolen modified car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a Polish person but is just a rod.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot rod is a car modified for extra speed and power, which is what souped-up means.

clue.text: Place for prisoner that's done for misbehaving with gun?

indicators.note: misbehaving letters will not stay in order, so done and gun are mixed together

explanation.surface: Someone convicted for misbehaving with a gun ends up locked away.
explanation.definitionFit: A dungeon is an underground prison cell in a castle, a place to keep captives.

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
to run something is to organise it, so ran
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A bishop set up the church's local office.
explanation.definitionFit: A branch is a local office of a larger organisation such as a bank.

clue.text: Classified operations within Crete, strangely beginning to tell

indicators.note: the operations letters are placed inside the rest of the build
the beginning to a word is its first letter, here of tell
strangely says the letters of Crete are mixed up

parts.note: ops is the usual short form of operations

explanation.surface: Secret military operations on Crete start to be revealed.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue lists operations first, but the tell letter leads the answer: 'within' places them inside the T plus scrambled Crete, just after the T.
explanation.definitionFit: Classified documents are restricted to authorised readers, which is what top-secret means.

clue.text: Unenthusiastic in assembly over bringing in piano

indicators.note: bringing in means the piano letter is taken inside
over, in a down clue, says the assembly word is turned upside down

parts.note: a diet is a legislative assembly, as in the Diet of Japan
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: An assembly is lukewarm about acquiring a piano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns DIET into TEID, then P goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Tepid means lukewarm, and figuratively half-hearted or lacking enthusiasm.

clue.text: Racket made by small daughter at home

parts.note: D is the short form of daughter, as in family trees
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: A little girl is making a lot of noise in the house.
explanation.definitionFit: Racket and din are both synonyms for loud, confused noise.

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them closely
MA, Master of Arts, is a scholar's degree

explanation.surface: Someone is told to follow a scholar's teaching.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogma is a body of doctrine taught as authoritative, so a teaching.

parts.note: presto means at once, immediately

explanation.surface: Someone is told to name an English city at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Preston is a city in Lancashire in north-west England.

indicators.note: ignoring the black letter means leaving it out of the dog

parts.note: a beagle is a hound bred for hunting hares
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A hunting dog takes no notice of a black bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The eagle is a large bird of prey, an example of a bird.

clue.text: Very little wood, ultimately, and burnt remains

indicators.note: ultimately points at the last letter of wood

parts.note: ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: Only a scrap of a wood fire is left among the ashes.
explanation.definitionFit: A dash is a small quantity, as in a dash of milk, so very little.

parts.note: CH is the chess notation for check
plain speech is candid and frank

explanation.surface: Someone checks with a frank member of the clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaplain is a clergyman attached to an institution such as a school, hospital or regiment.
